It's $199 monthly .

[FrontBottom] First time I've seen trackingroo. Thanks!
[justanotherjoe] The 2x 200w panel deal is worth it though, can even get the full 200w per panel (on a good day) as I have several of these already.
https://www.woolworths.com.au/shop/productdetails/1125798017…

[M911] If you join the mailing list you will get 2-3 emails a day sometime even about the same sale
[OBH] Don't forget spam text messages if you ever buy anything
[kml22] No, it's a bit higher, which exceeds the power station's strict 10A input limit on the C800.
[eDust] Could you cover (fold up) part of this panel to reduce the current?
[guitargeek89] No need to. The C800 will regulate itself. This will work with the c800. Only restriction is max open circuit voltage of 60v.
[guitargeek89] This is incorrect. Not how electronics works.
[team teri] Seeing how often it drops to $199, I'd suggest to hold out for a 30% cashback deal on Everyday Market, works out a lot better than just $15 off.
[Aceofspades] I did this about a week ago.$59.70 cashback. 12.55 shipping
[LukeOz83] As cheap as it seems, its not a great deal and you'll only end up with a headache. Some come faulty from factory and if you get one that actually produces some good numbers, it will deteriorate faster than you'd expect.
You may think that it works because it charges your battery, but meter may show you that you're only getting 100W or less. Its because these are very fragile and any slight bending will damage them enough to drop the charge.
This is probably the only thing I wouldn't buy from Kings (or other sellers tbh) ever again.
[heshanh] bought one few months ago the the 240w blanket. Been using it and the most ive been able to get from it is 196w on a decent full sunny day.
however between 8am - 4pm was able to make just over 500w to charge 2nd battery in the car
[LukeOz83] I had 2 240W and 4 120W over the time. First 240W produced 100W at most, so was sent another one after proving its not charging. Second one worked for about 6 months before it started dropping its output.
The smaller ones were about the same, in the end I measured around 40W on all of them.
Problem is that sopar panels are very fragile and the constant bending doesnt help. If its not the actual panel part where you break the connections inside the panel itself, the contacts between the tiles break as well. Found out that by shading some I had still the same output.
[9839002] Yeah the dream of the blanket is great but the reality is they're a shitty solution. Even the ARB ones never come close to rated output and the interconnecting wires wear out from folding.
Better solutions for solar power exist.
[peter6775] I had the 200w blanket a couple of years ago. It was significantly lower in capacity than stated and the wires were fragile- as there was additional sheath or protection. Didn’t last too long - didn’t want to go through the return to base and test etc.
Bought a Boab brand and has been good .
[Mums Poop Sock] I use the 140? Watt one and it serves me well and puts out a solids 8amps in ideal conditions.
[gtech] Another thing to consider is how they are wired, a lot of the cheap panels/blanked that are wired/structured in a serial (?) manner meaning that a bit of shading drops your output between 60-80%. Had a 1.2 X 0.7m panel that was outputting 25-35w out 160w because it had a A4 size shade in one corner.
